public_rationale: The claim is read as a description of AI in calendar 2025. Two preprints published in October 2025 tested 2025 models, and both fit the claim. The Remote Labor Index (submitted 30 Oct 2025) tests AI agents on real-world projects to measure end-to-end performance. The best agent reached an automation rate of 2.5% (e1). So agents rarely completed whole projects. GDPval (submitted 5 Oct 2025) builds its tasks from the work of professionals with an average of 14 years' experience (e3). On its 220-task gold subset, 47.6% of deliverables from Claude Opus 4.1, the best model there, were graded as better than or as good as the human deliverable (e2). That is a real share of tasks at expert level, but it is not all of them. Neither study shows AI routinely completing whole jobs end to end, matching experts on nearly all tasks, or doing almost none of the work. Those are the contract's tests for contradiction.
limitations: The benchmarks measure tasks and projects, not junior or senior job titles. They do not measure judgement directly.
'Often' is not quantified. Whether a match rate near half counts as 'often lacks' is a matter of degree.

The GDPval text gives 47.6% for Claude Opus 4.1, but the same section also says model deliverables matched or beat experts in 'just over half' of tasks. The evidence does not settle which figure applies to which comparison.
Both studies came out after the post (23 Aug 2025), though they test models from 2025.
The result covers 2025 only. It says nothing about later models.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI can do some but often not all junior employee work and often lacks senior employees' judgement.

statement.excerpt: AI can do at least some of the work that junior employeess can do, but often not all of it, and AI often lacks the judgement of senior employees.
statement.document_title: AI, layoffs, productivity and The Klarna Effect

from_speaker: AI can do at least some of the work that junior employees can do
but often not all of it
AI often lacks the judgement of senior employees
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in 2025, AI systems could do a real share of workplace tasks, but often could not complete whole jobs or projects end to end, and often fell short of experienced professionals' quality or judgment.
The period is the state of AI around the post, read as calendar 2025. Capability tests of the models available then were published in September–October 2025.
criteria.support_condition: 2025 evaluations show AI matching humans on a meaningful share of tasks, while failing on many whole projects or falling short of experts on a large share of tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: 2025 evaluations show AI routinely completing whole junior roles end to end and matching senior professionals on nearly all tasks, or doing almost none of the work.
